title: People’s Mañanera September 30
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Housing for Well-Being: A Right Made Real  
** In Zacatecas, 18 homes were delivered. The state’s goal is to build 27,500
homes, and 30 percent of the target has already been reached. This is how a
policy that seeks to turn the right to housing into a tangible family asset is
moving forward.

**Humanistic Environmentalism: Well-Being with Environmental Justice  
** Mexico is moving forward with a policy that protects people and nature,
involving a 35% reduction in emissions and the use of 38% renewable energy by
2030. The “Sembrando Vida” (Sowing Life) initiative involves sowing 75 million
plants across 36,000 hectares with the help of 415,000 growers.

**Water Is a Right, Not a Commodity  
** 5 billion cubic meters of water were recovered, equivalent to the annual
supply for 90 million people. With an investment of more than 80 billion pesos
(US$4.45 billion), 17 strategic projects are moving forward; and with 20
billion pesos (US$1.11 billion) three rivers are being cleaned up, benefitting
25 million people.

**One Homeland, One Flag  
** The Senate approved the constitutional reform requiring Presidential and
gubernatorial candidates to hold only Mexican citizenship. President Claudia
Sheinbaum explained that “the presidents of Mexico can only have one flag, one
homeland.”

**Freedom of Expression, with a Sense of History  
** Regarding former president Felipe Calderón’s participation in a Latin
American right-wing forum, Sheinbaum recalled the García Luna case and the
rise in homicides during his six-year term in office. She quipped, “He’s going
to talk about democracy,” but emphasized that “there is nevertheless maximum
freedom of expression” in the country.

**Lie Detector**

  * It is not true that an “anti-meme law” will be created that will criminalize satire and undermine freedom of expression.
  * It is not true that Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco “diverted” the discussion from security issues in Mexico during his address to the UN General Assembly.
  * It is not true that the Tulum archaeological site has been privatized.
  * It is not true that journalists “are receiving death threats” from the Mexican government.
  * It is not true that the Mexican government will give away “Well-Being Motorcycles” to the public through a new social program.
